title: "I will send you Elijah the prophet before the great and terrible day of the LORD" (Mal 4:4–6)
speaker: The LORD
description: Remember the law of Moses given at Horeb; the LORD will send Elijah before the great and terrible day, to turn the hearts of fathers to children and children to fathers, lest he strike the land with a curse.

interpretations.label: Fulfilled in John the Baptist, who came in the spirit and power of Elijah
proponents: D. Guzik (figuratively in John; completely before the second coming)
interpretations.summary: Textual reasoning: Jesus identifies John as "Elijah who is to come", and Luke speaks of John in the spirit and power of Elijah, turning fathers' hearts to children. Objection: John himself denied being Elijah (John 1:21); Smith reads the verses as expecting Elijah in person and as a later gloss.

interpretations.label: A later gloss expecting Elijah himself, taken up in Jewish eschatology
interpretations.summary: Textual reasoning: vv. 5–6 reopen a closed subject and view the day differently (all classes need purification); they probably reflect a later, Hellenising age; Elijah was chosen perhaps because he escaped death; the first known reference to him as forerunner (cf. Enoch 90; the Gospels).
